question: An agent is configured with dozens of MCP tools across several servers, and the team notices that tool definitions are consuming a large share of the context window on every turn even when most tools go unused. What is the most direct way to address this?
options: A) Set permissionMode to "bypassPermissions" so fewer messages are exchanged per turn
B) Move every MCP server from stdio to HTTP transport to reduce payload size
C) Enable tool search so definitions are withheld from context and loaded only when Claude needs them
D) Reduce MCP_TIMEOUT so unused server connections close faster
correct_answers: C) Enable tool search so definitions are withheld from context and loaded only when Claude needs them
explanations: Incorrect. bypassPermissions changes permission prompting behavior; it has no effect on how many tool definitions are loaded into context.
Incorrect. Transport type affects how the agent communicates with a server process, not how much context space tool definitions occupy.
Correct. Tool search withholds tool definitions from context by default and loads only the ones Claude needs for a given turn, directly reducing context consumption from a large tool set.
Incorrect. MCP_TIMEOUT controls how long the SDK waits for a server connection to establish, not the size of tool definitions kept in context.
